news.title: SpaceX signs a binding ~$40B GPU lease financing with an Apollo-managed entity
news.summary: A Monday regulatory filing says an Apollo-managed entity will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to SpaceX for about five to five-and-a-quarter years from each tranche's delivery. SpaceX called it the largest committed GPU financing; it expects the deal to close by year-end, with leases starting in the first half of 2027. SPCX closed down 0.4% at $146.90.

news.title: Musk accuses Ukraine of violating Starlink terms with drone strikes; Ukraine denies it
news.summary: Musk said Ukraine's military used the commercial Starlink service for offensive drone strikes and that the 'loophole was closed last week'. Ukrainian officials denied misuse, and President Zelenskyy said the new satellite restrictions had been lifted and Starshield access is back to normal.

news.title: SpaceX closes $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, Musk says
news.summary: Musk said on X that SpaceX closed $40B of mostly callable debt financing for GPUs arriving in Q1–Q2 2027 ("not a major factor this quarter"), crediting its investment-grade status and Starlink/launch revenue. No lenders, pricing or terms were disclosed; Bloomberg had reported a Goldman-led, off-balance-sheet SPV structure with Apollo. Musk also said 200+ neoclouds face "guppy-level death and consolidation" and that SpaceX won't buy any.

news.title: SpaceX completes full-duration 33-engine static fire of Booster 22 ahead of Starship Flight 15
news.summary: The V3 Super Heavy assigned to Starship Flight 15 fired all 33 Raptor 3 engines on Pad 2 at Starbase on Sunday morning. Flight 15 is targeted no earlier than Nov. 8; no FAA license has been issued yet.

news.title: US military gives SpaceX access to sensitive space-tracking data
news.summary: The U.S. military granted SpaceX access to restricted orbital-tracking data, giving it an edge in tracking objects in orbit and raising national-security and space-traffic-control concerns among industry observers.

news.title: After SpaceX restores high-speed service, Musk says Ukraine violated Starlink agreement
news.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry said Starlink and Starshield connections were restored on equipment moving above 400 km/h after more than a week of throttling that disrupted drone operations. Musk then said SpaceX had closed a "loophole" because Ukraine's military used Starlink, a civilian service, for offensive drone strikes, adding that Starshield is controlled by the U.S. government.

news.title: Space Force shifts missile-warning and cislunar missions from Vulcan to Falcon Heavy
news.summary: Citing Vulcan delays, the Space Force moved a Next-Gen OPIR missile-warning satellite, a cislunar surveillance payload stack, three GPS launches and an SDA mission from United Launch Alliance to SpaceX rockets; ULA will receive later SpaceX payloads in return.

news.title: Telecom stocks wobble after report SpaceX is in talks for at least 80,000 cell sites
news.summary: Bloomberg reported late Thursday that SpaceX is negotiating access to at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites, including with Crown Castle, to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. AT&T fell 5.6%, T-Mobile 5% and Verizon 1.6%, while Crown Castle jumped 11.6%; Bernstein said the competitive impact may be years away. SPCX rose 1.9% to $147.49.

news.title: Musk's public endorsement of a SpaceX–Tesla deal may throw a wrench in talks
news.summary: Musk's comments about a potential $3.5 trillion combination rattled some insiders, who worry it could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay the process by several weeks, a source said. Talks are early; SpaceX approached Tesla in recent weeks, and structures under discussion include a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla or a new holding company, possibly all-stock.

news.title: Silicon Valley Democrats demand probe of Starlink restrictions in Ukraine
news.summary: House Democrats asked the White House to investigate the throttling of Starshield, the military version of Starlink, in Ukraine; Ukrainian officials said speed limits on drone-mounted receivers remained despite President Trump saying service was restored. The letter signals scrutiny of federal funding for Musk's companies if Democrats win the House on Nov. 3.

news.title: SpaceX declines three Space Force launch contracts; Starship Flight 15 targeted for November
news.summary: Citing Politico, Ars reports SpaceX declined to bid on three National Security Space Launch missions as it stops signing new Falcon 9/Falcon Heavy contracts. Shotwell said SpaceX expects the Flight 15 license to include return-to-launch-site tower catches of both stages; Musk disputed a NASA safety panel estimate of about 22 refuelings for a lunar landing, saying 6 to 8.

news.title: With earnings done, SpaceX–Tesla merger chatter takes center stage
news.summary: A tie-up faces negotiations, shareholder votes and U.S. and foreign regulatory reviews; Musk said Tesla would need a 50% vote of all shares. William Blair called the push about control rather than a material opportunity, while former Tesla director Steve Westly expects a proposal quickly, ideally before the midterms. SpaceX's 9% drop put it back below its post-debut opening price.
